text.p: On commodity markets on Friday, copper prices firmed again on aggressive shortcovering despite an unexpected stocks increase.
Gold prices also firmed again slightly overall in London and New York on Friday as funds took profits on more short positions against a backdrop of good demand for bullion.
Wheat prices surged on fund buying while oil prices fell on news a U.S. refinery would open sooner than expected.
The CRB index closed down 0.13 at 241.23.
Copper finished substantially firmer on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday, hanging on to most of the gains from a brisk early rally.

Technical buying and aggressive short covering took copper to fresh 8-1/2 month highs despite an unexpected stocks increase of 1,875 tonnes. It was at $2,366 per tonne at the afternoon kerb close, off the day's $2,375 high but nevertheless up $38 from Thursday's finish. Expectations that Chinese demand was on the rise in the near term was seen leading to tightening in the market in future, piquing market interest, analysts said.
Aluminium was also notably firmer after breaching resistance around $1,615, thereby triggering buy-stops.
A drawdown of 2,400 tonnes in LME stocks, along with stronger copper, helped aluminium.
It ended the kerb at the day's highs of $1,631, which was $24 firmer than on Thursday.
The other base metals exhibited less buoyancy.

Nickel finished off its highs, drifting below the $7,900 level to close just $25 firmer at $7,875. Tin and zinc ended slightly lower after bids to follow copper higher failed amid lack of interest and follow through buying. Zinc fell $5 to $1,211. Alloy was last a firmer $1,550, versus $1,532/35.

CBOT wheat futures surged in late dealings and ended sharply higher on fund buying tied to options-related arbitrage trading, traders said on Friday. Wheat closed nine to 10-1/2 cents higher, with March up 9-1/4 at $3.73 per bushel and new-crop July 9-3/4 cents higher at $3.63.

NYMEX gasoline led oil prices to a lower finish Friday on the prospect of more supply, as a large refinery owned by Tosco Corp was said to be restarting sooner than expected. April crude settled 30 cents lower at $21.39 a barrel as crude was sold in favor of heating oil after a recent sharp fall in the heating-to-crude crack spread.
New York precious metals futures ended mixed Friday, but gold extended its recovery for the eighth day in a row,

COMEX April gold ended up $1.50 an ounce at $354.10, after seeing an 18 day intraday high at $356.80. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $351.90/40 an ounce compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $353.30 and the New York close Thursday at $350.40/90.

With commodity funds taking profits on short positions, physical gold demand picking up, and the US dollar and US stockmarket both seeing a downward correction this week, some investors were being tempted back into precious metals, traders said.
